note: Matches the starting-point half of the ICP cleanly and fails the commercial half. Neglected health is textbook: a competitive equestrian until 24 who moved into office work and never replaced it — 'I tried to keep up doing some stuff, but never figured out something that was working fine for me' — with work explicitly fine ('work is doing fine, I'm doing great at work and everything is set up over there') and health the area left behind. Good to great is his own framing: at 80 kg and 1.80 m he says 'I don't think I'm that big or that far off from where I want to go', wants to see his abs rather than transform, and explicitly rejects the bodybuilder end. Not deconditioned holds on both halves — a normal BMI, training most days at home, and no aversion to exercise, only to gyms specifically. Successful is not evidenced: he describes an office desk role and a busy schedule but never states an occupation, and nothing in the transcript supports business owner, physician or equivalent. Income fails on the affordability test as run: around €10k liquid against €5-10k of committed upcoming expenses, a price expectation below $6,000, and a refusal to commit until his bank adviser confirms it. Two observations for the rollup. First, this prospect had received no price pre-framing at all — 'the question I have, because I haven't seen it anywhere, is the price' — which converts an income question into a surprise objection, and the ICP file's own third observation about income screening applies directly. Second, an unnamed chronic intestinal condition was disclosed in the first three minutes and no ICP criterion would have surfaced it, which is now the fourth call in this batch to demonstrate that the stated ICP has no clinical screen.
